question: Estimate the size of the working women segment in India (formal employment) and their consumer market.
idealClarificationQuestions: Formally employed women (salaried + own business)? Yes.
Their annual consumer spending power? Yes.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Frame the approach
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Working women population × disposable income × consumer spend share.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Indian women in formal/salaried employment: ~13M (per generalist Q19).

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Total addressable working women: ~38M (note: distinct from agriculture/informal labor).

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Disposable income (after savings, family expenses): ~30% = ₹1-1.2L per woman.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Categories: beauty + fashion + electronics + finance + auto = bulk of this spend.

benchmarkAssumptions.value: ~₹3-4 lakh (mix of corporate executives at ₹15L+ and SMB workers at ₹2L).

benchmarkAssumptions.parameter: Total consumer market driven by working women
benchmarkAssumptions.value: 38M × ₹1.1L = ~₹42 lakh Cr potential spend, of which actually spent on personal/discretionary: ~₹10 lakh Cr.

calculationFlow: Average annual earnings: ~₹3-4 lakh (mix of corporate executives at ₹15L+ and SMB workers at ₹2L).
Disposable income (after savings, family expenses): ~30% = ₹1-1.2L per woman.
Total consumer market driven by working women: 38M × ₹1.1L = ~₹42 lakh Cr potential spend, of which actually spent on personal/discretionary: ~₹10 lakh Cr.
Categories: beauty + fashion + electronics + finance + auto = bulk of this spend.

finalAnswerRange.ideal: Total consumer market driven by working women: 38M × ₹1.1L = ~₹42 lakh Cr potential spend, of which actually spent on personal/discretionary: ~₹10 lakh Cr.
